newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINN PORT TO FAVOUR PRIVATE OPERATORS.
newsitem.headline: TALLINN PORT TO FAVOUR PRIVATE OPERATORS.

text.p: The Estonian government on Tuesday approved the development plan of the state-owned Tallinn Port, which sees its future as a state enterprise with private operators.
"Private enterprises are able to guarantee the turnover of goods when the infrastructure is there," Communications Minister Raivo Vare told a news conference.
The development plan also calls for the renting of several terminals to private firms and the construction of a container terminal, Vare said.
Vare said the state has no plans to privatise its stake in Tallinn Port now, but added that this has not been ruled out in the long-term.
"Today there is no direct economic need to privatise the shares," Vare said.
"Tallinn Port is a key object in Estonia taking into account that most transit goes through its ports," Vare said.
The port reloaded 14 million tonnes of goods and served 4.2 million passengers last year, Vare said, adding that these totals can be raised by 70 to 80 percent.
